threads.body: [Javaagent] For a rejected absolute target such as `http://example.com?AWSAccessKeyId=/secret%%`, the first slash after the authority belongs to the query, so this emits `/secret%%` as `url.path` and omits `url.query`. This bypasses the default query-value redaction for `AWSAccessKeyId`. Check the query boundary before selecting a path slash, and preserve the query when the absolute target has no path.

replies.body: Fixed in ef19989046: the authority now ends at the first `/`, `?` or `#`, so a target with a query but no path reports `url.query` and no `url.path`. Added `absoluteTargetWithoutPathIsTraced` covering `http://example.com?q=/%%`.

replies.body: Fixed in b32e10edf5: a target counts as absolute-form only when it starts with a valid scheme (`ALPHA *( ALPHA / DIGIT / "+" / "-" / "." )`) followed by `://`. `getUrlScheme` and `pathAndQuery` share that check. The regression test is `targetWithoutValidSchemeIsNotAbsolute`.

threads.body: [Javaagent] A rejected target such as `/path?AWSAccessKeyId=first#&AWSAccessKeyId=secret` retains its fragment in `url.query`, and `UrlQuerySanitizer` preserves everything after `#`, leaving the second value unredacted. Path-only targets also expose the fragment in `url.path`. Strip everything from the first raw `#` before extracting either component, for both origin-form and absolute-form targets.

replies.body: Fixed in b32e10edf5: everything from the first `#` is dropped before the scheme, path or query is extracted, for both origin-form and absolute-form targets. The regression test is `fragmentOfRejectedTargetIsDropped`.

threads.body: Pekko preserves literal control characters in rejected targets. These getters can pass them through to `url.path` or `url.query`, and the `logging` exporter writes string attributes unescaped. That can alter terminal log output. Please omit both URL attributes when the target contains control characters.

replies.body: Fixed in 4341312370: `pathAndQuery` returns null when the target, after the fragment is dropped, contains any `Character.isISOControl` character (C0, DEL and C1), so neither `url.path` nor `url.query` is reported. The regression test is `targetWithControlCharactersIsNotReported`.

threads.body: Pekko renders an IPv6 `CONNECT` authority with a leading `//` before passing it to the rejection handler. This branch treats the whole authority as `url.path` before reaching the `CONNECT` guard. Move the guard before the leading-slash branch and add an IPv6 case alongside the hostname test.

replies.body: Fixed in 4341312370: the CONNECT check is now the first thing in `pathAndQuery`, so a CONNECT target never yields a path or query, whatever form pekko-http renders it in. `ipv6ConnectRequestIsTraced` covers `[::1]:443` alongside the hostname case.

Applied in f21836dbb6: a target that starts with `//` and has no later `/` or `?` is skipped. The regression test is `renderedAuthorityIsNotReported`, which sends `GET user@[::1]:80 HTTP/1.0` without a Host header. Also picked up your `PER_CLASS` commit, thanks.

threads.body: For `GET //%% HTTP/1.1`, this guard mistakes the malformed origin-form target for a rendered authority and drops `url.path`; adding `?q=1` makes the same path reappear. Pekko's [parser reads the target before the protocol](https://github.com/apache/pekko-http/blob/50d97ed71ba67716487c19ded9f8712e40b17e36/http-core/src/main/scala/org/apache/pekko/http/impl/engine/parsing/HttpRequestParser.scala#L102-L108), while [rendered rejection contexts include a protocol](https://github.com/apache/pekko-http/blob/50d97ed71ba67716487c19ded9f8712e40b17e36/http-core/src/main/scala/org/apache/pekko/http/impl/engine/server/HttpServerBluePrint.scala#L284-L290) (upstream default branch). Restrict this exclusion to contexts with a parsed protocol, and add a regression for the queryless malformed target.

replies.body: Fixed in fa02be2738: the rendered-authority guard now applies only when the context has a protocol. pekko-http renders a target only for a request line it parsed up to the protocol, so without one the target is what the client sent and a leading `//` starts its path. The regression test is `malformedPathWithLeadingDoubleSlashIsReported`, which sends `GET //%% HTTP/1.1` and expects `url.path` of `//%%`; `renderedAuthorityIsNotReported` still passes.

threads.body: For `GET //admin HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n` without a Host header, this guard drops the known `url.path`, while adding `?q=1` makes the same path reappear. The [Pekko parser retains both the raw target and parsed protocol for this rejection](https://github.com/apache/pekko-http/blob/b6a11a0b000c38191fbb6088dd96cc408b68dfde/http-core/src/main/scala/org/apache/pekko/http/impl/engine/parsing/HttpRequestParser.scala#L267-L279), so protocol presence does not identify a rendered authority. Track whether the target came from parsing or URI rendering before applying this exclusion, and add a missing-Host regression while preserving the rendered-authority userinfo protection.

replies.body:
Leaving this as it is. The observation is right: a missing `Host` on HTTP/1.1 is rejected by the parser, so the context has the raw `//admin` and a protocol, and `url.path` is dropped. But `IllegalRequestContext` only carries the method, target and protocol, with nothing to say whether the target is what the client sent or a URI pekko-http rendered, so the instrumentation cannot track that. Once a protocol is present, a raw `//admin` path and an authority rendered as `//admin` or `//user@host` are the same string. A rendered one is not limited to HTTP/1.0 either, an HTTP/1.1 request with an empty `Host` header gets there too, so the protocol version does not separate them.

Given that, the guard stays conservative: a `//segment` target with no later `/` or `?` is not reported when a protocol was parsed, at the cost of losing `url.path` for that shape of path on rejections after the request line. That seems the better side to err on than exporting userinfo. The only alternative I can see is keying on the text of the effective-URI error message, which would silently stop protecting if pekko-http reworded it.

Applied in 211c7c7930: `PekkoHttpParsingErrorRequest` no longer holds the `ErrorInfo`. The field, `info()`, the import and the constructor argument are gone, the call site in `PekkoHttpParsingErrorSingletons` is updated and the class Javadoc no longer mentions it. No new tests, the existing parsing error tests pass on pekko-http 1.x and 2.x.

Applied in 211c7c7930: both getters now pass `request.protocol()` straight to `HttpProtocolUtil.getProtocol` / `getVersion`. No new tests, the existing assertions on `network.protocol.version` being present or absent still pass.

[Simplification] There's no need to build HOCON text with escaped quotes and a `ConfigFactory.load()` fallback. You can set the handler with `ServerSettings(system).withParsingErrorHandler(...)` and bind through `newServerAt(...).withSettings(...)`. `customHandlerIsTraced` in `PekkoHttpServerParsingErrorTest` already does it this way. This test only runs on Pekko 2, so it doesn't need the `PekkoHttpTestBinding` indirection. After this change, the `com.typesafe.config.ConfigFactory` import is unused and can be removed. You may also need to import `org.apache.pekko.http.scaladsl.Http` if it isn't already imported.

```suggestion
    implicit val system: ActorSystem = ActorSystem("parsing-error-handler-test")
    try {
      val handler: HttpRequest => HttpResponse = _ => HttpResponse()
      val settings =
        ServerSettings(system).withParsingErrorHandler(handlerClass.getName)
      val binding =
        Await.result(
          Http()
            .newServerAt("localhost", 0)
            .withSettings(settings)
            .bindSync(handler),
          10.seconds
        )
```
